title: WebRTC SFU broadcast, receiver groups and E2EE semantic fan-out
goal: Extend Ananta from its current pair-oriented WebRTC DataChannel and opaque Hub Relay transport into an optional multi-participant SFU topology. A sender uploads each media or semantic source stream once; an SFU or fan-out coordinator forwards the same encrypted payload to many authorized receivers, while receiver groups, per-peer adaptation, E2EE key epochs, congestion control, backpressure and fallback remain deterministic and measurable.

codebase_alignment.current_transport: frontend-angular/src/app/services/webrtc-transport.service.ts currently exposes one sessionId, one WebrtcSessionService, a single mode state and a DataChannel-or-Hub-Relay decision. It has no participant collection, publication/subscription model or SFU abstraction.
codebase_alignment.current_datachannel_path: WebrtcTransportService.send() and sendView() route one typed payload into WebrtcSessionService or POST it to the session relay. Existing behavior must remain compatible for pair sessions.
codebase_alignment.current_relay: Hub Relay polling is interval-based, session-scoped and forwards bounded opaque envelopes. It is a reliability fallback, not a scalable realtime SFU.
codebase_alignment.pair_view: docs/architecture/pair-view-sync.md explicitly lists multi-participant n>2 as out of scope. This todo supplies the missing group topology without replacing pair-view contracts.
codebase_alignment.semantic_stream_parent: The semantic WebRTC todo already plans signed capabilities, compute-quality contracts, task leases, semantic frames, reconstruction reports and strict-E2EE routing. Reuse these contracts and epochs.
codebase_alignment.semantic_speech_parent: The semantic speech todo already plans prioritized transcripts, delayed encrypted audio, per-listener reconstruction and 100-listener benchmarks. Broadcast must support shared and receiver-specific layers.
known_gaps: No SFU or media publication/subscription abstraction is implemented.
No distinction exists between a shared payload sent identically to all receivers and receiver-specific correction or adaptation payloads.
No receiver groups, subscription filters, publication permissions or fan-out leases exist.
No group E2EE key-epoch contract exists for membership changes.
No per-receiver congestion state or quality-layer selection exists.
No server egress, TURN amplification or fan-out backpressure accounting exists.
No deterministic fallback topology exists between SFU, peer mesh, Hub Relay and one-way streaming/CDN paths.

principles: WebRTC does not provide IP multicast; server egress remains approximately proportional to receiver count.
The sender should upload one shared publication per selected quality or semantic layer, not one copy per receiver.
Shared data and receiver-specific data must use separate channels and accounting.
The SFU forwards encrypted media and semantic payloads without requiring plaintext under strict E2EE.
Membership, publication, subscription and key changes are versioned and epoch-bound.
A weak receiver must not force every receiver onto its lowest quality.
Control, transcript, interruption and recovery messages take priority over media residuals and bulk training synchronization.
The realtime forwarding path must never run unbounded inference or blocking training work.
Existing two-peer behavior remains the default-compatible path until group mode is explicitly enabled.
Capacity planning must include peak fallback traffic, not only optimized semantic averages.
non_goals: Do not claim that SFU fan-out is true network multicast.
Do not make the Hub polling relay the primary path for large live rooms.
Do not decrypt strict-E2EE media or semantic payloads in the SFU.
Do not duplicate an identical encoded stream separately at the sender for each receiver.
Do not require every participant to publish audio and video in webinar mode.
Do not mix model training workloads into the SFU packet-forwarding process.
Do not promise fixed participant counts without measured CPU, network, TURN and file-descriptor limits.

target_topologies.pair_legacy: Existing direct WebRTC connection with opaque Hub Relay fallback.
target_topologies.small_mesh: Optional direct peer mesh for very small trusted groups where negotiated limits permit it.
target_topologies.sfu_room: Publish once to SFU; SFU forwards selected encrypted layers to authorized subscribers.
target_topologies.webinar: One or few publishers, many mostly receive-only participants, prioritized control/transcript channels.
target_topologies.semantic_broadcast: One shared semantic/transcript/reference publication plus per-receiver reconstruction reports and selective correction streams.
target_topologies.degraded_relay: Bounded Hub Relay for control and recovery only when realtime DataChannels fail.
target_topologies.large_one_way: Optional WebRTC ingest with non-interactive distribution path evaluated separately when receiver counts exceed SFU economics.

milestones.title: Topology and contracts
milestones.exit: Publication, subscription, room, receiver-group and key-epoch schemas are approved.

milestones.title: Three-peer SFU MVP
milestones.exit: One publisher sends once and two receivers consume through an SFU adapter with E2EE payload opacity.

milestones.title: Layered and semantic fan-out
milestones.exit: Shared layers and receiver-specific corrections are routed independently.

milestones.title: Dynamic rooms
milestones.exit: Join, leave, revoke, rekey, reconnect and SFU failover work deterministically.

milestones.title: Scale and observability
milestones.exit: 100-receiver benchmarks, backpressure, TURN and egress budgets pass.

milestones.title: Controlled rollout
milestones.exit: Feature flags, compatibility, security review and fallback capacity are release-ready.

tasks.title: Document SFU topology, trust boundaries and terminology
tasks.description: Define publisher, publication, subscriber, receiver group, SFU node, TURN relay, Hub coordinator, strict-E2EE and trusted-server profiles. Explicitly separate server-side fan-out from true multicast.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture shows ingress once per publication layer and separate egress per receiver.
Trust boundaries for browser, SFU, TURN, Hub, AI-Snake and optional compute worker are explicit.
Pair, mesh, SFU, webinar, degraded relay and large one-way topologies are compared.
Server egress and TURN amplification are identified as scaling constraints.
Strict-E2EE states that SFU routing does not require plaintext content.
Realtime forwarding and offline model training are separate processes and resource pools.

tasks.title: Select and isolate an SFU adapter boundary
tasks.description: Define a vendor-neutral interface for room creation, token issuance, publication, subscription, layer selection, participant events and node health. Evaluate implementation candidates separately without leaking vendor objects into application contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Application contracts contain no vendor-specific room, track or token classes.
Adapter declares support for E2EE insertable streams, simulcast/SVC, DataChannel and server metrics.
Unsupported capabilities fail through stable reason codes.
A deterministic mock adapter supports CI and local tests.
Deployment, licensing, operational complexity and required ports are documented.
Existing pair WebRTC service remains usable without the SFU dependency.

tasks.title: Create versioned room, publication and subscription schemas
tasks.description: Add bounded, signed and replay-resistant schemas for group sessions and fan-out routing.
acceptance_criteria: Every authoritative contract contains version, room/session identity, epoch, expiry and signer identity.
Arrays, labels, layers, members and metadata have explicit count and byte limits.
Publication and subscription permissions are independent and default-deny.
Unknown security-sensitive properties are rejected.
Python and TypeScript validators share a conformance fixture corpus.
Fixtures cover stale epochs, replay, oversized groups, unauthorized subscription and malformed layer selection.

tasks.title: Refactor transport into pair and room session abstractions
tasks.description: Preserve the current pair-session facade while introducing explicit pair and room session implementations with participant collections, publications and subscriptions.
acceptance_criteria: Existing open(sessionId, isInitiator), send and sendView call paths remain backward compatible or receive a documented adapter.
Room mode supports multiple participants and concurrent publications without global singleton peer state.
Pair and room lifecycles expose deterministic connecting, connected, degraded, reconnecting, failed and closed states.
Subscriptions are disposed on leave and do not leak RxJS listeners or peer connections.
Transport mode is represented per room/session rather than as one global value.
Unit tests cover simultaneous pair and room sessions.

tasks.title: Implement authenticated room membership and role policy
tasks.description: Create room admission, join, leave, role, permission, expiry and revocation handling. Roles include host, publisher, subscriber, moderator, validator and compute contributor without implying one another.
acceptance_criteria: Joining requires authenticated, room-scoped admission.
Publish and subscribe grants are separate and direction-specific.
Receive-only webinar participants cannot publish unless explicitly promoted.
Revocation reaches the SFU adapter within a bounded timeout.
Membership changes increment an epoch and trigger key-policy evaluation.
Audit logs contain identities and reason codes but no media plaintext.

tasks.title: Implement publication and subscription lifecycle
tasks.description: Allow authorized publishers to create audio, video, data and semantic publications and receivers to subscribe, pause, resume, switch layers and unsubscribe.
acceptance_criteria: A publisher sends one copy per produced layer to the SFU regardless of subscriber count.
Each subscriber may independently select compatible layers.
Publication identity survives temporary reconnect without accepting stale instances.
Duplicate publish or subscribe requests are idempotent.
Unpublished or revoked streams cannot remain subscribed.
Metrics expose publisher ingress and aggregate receiver egress separately.

tasks.title: Add simulcast and scalable-layer selection
tasks.description: Publish bounded quality layers and let each subscriber receive an independently selected layer based on viewport, bandwidth, packet loss, CPU and user policy.
acceptance_criteria: Layer selection is per subscriber and does not globally downgrade the room.
Audio, screen share, camera and semantic references use separate policies.
Hysteresis and dwell times prevent rapid layer oscillation.
Hidden or thumbnail video may suspend high layers.
Layer changes preserve keyframe/recovery correctness.
Unsupported simulcast/SVC falls back to a documented single-layer profile.

tasks.title: Create receiver groups and shared fan-out routes
tasks.description: Group receivers with identical authorization and layer requirements so routing decisions and shared semantic payloads can be computed once while transport egress remains per receiver.
acceptance_criteria: Group membership is derived from explicit policy attributes and a stable member digest.
A receiver is never grouped across incompatible consent, key epoch or privacy scopes.
Group recomputation is bounded and incremental on join, leave or policy change.
Shared payload processing occurs once per compatible group, not once per receiver.
Actual network delivery remains separately metered per receiver.
Group failure cannot authorize a receiver that was not individually admitted.

tasks.title: Separate shared semantic layers from receiver-specific corrections
tasks.description: Fan out transcript, scene graph, reference frame and shared model metadata once per receiver group, while reconstruction reports, missing references and personalized residuals remain private per receiver.
acceptance_criteria: Shared and receiver-specific message kinds are enumerated and validated.
A personalized correction can never be broadcast to another receiver.
Receiver reports are aggregated only into privacy-approved statistics.
Shared references are content-addressed and deduplicated per publication epoch.
Missing references trigger selective recovery rather than a room-wide reset.
Ordinary encrypted media remains available as fallback per receiver.

tasks.title: Add speech transcript broadcast and private personalization channels
tasks.description: Broadcast authoritative transcript revisions, timing and shared delayed-audio references to authorized listener groups, while pair-personalized model data, local reconstruction reports and training evidence remain scoped.
acceptance_criteria: Transcript revisions and interruption markers use the highest-priority reliable channel.
One speaker transcript can reach many authorized listeners without sender-side duplication.
Pair-specific speaker adapters and training evidence are never group-broadcast by default.
Listeners may independently choose captions, generic synthesis, personalized synthesis or original audio.
A slow listener does not delay transcript delivery to others.
Consent changes immediately alter group membership and future fan-out.

tasks.title: Implement group E2EE epochs and membership rekeying
tasks.description: Bind encrypted publications to membership epochs and rotate access when participants join, leave or lose permission, without exposing media keys to the SFU.
acceptance_criteria: New members cannot decrypt past epochs unless policy explicitly permits history.
Removed members cannot decrypt future epochs.
Rekey messages are authenticated, replay-protected and bounded.
SFU routing identifiers reveal no media key material.
Temporary key-distribution failure degrades safely without accepting stale membership.
Tests cover rapid churn, reconnect, malicious replay and simultaneous membership changes.

tasks.title: Add congestion control, queue priority and fan-out backpressure
tasks.description: Prevent slow receivers or overloaded SFU nodes from growing unbounded queues. Degrade low-priority layers before dropping control, transcript or recovery traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Byte, message, age and buffered-duration limits exist per receiver and traffic class.
Priority order is deterministic and documented.
Slow receivers are isolated, layer-downgraded or disconnected without blocking others.
Bulk training sync pauses before realtime media is degraded.
Dropped messages emit bounded reason-coded metrics.
Load tests demonstrate bounded memory during sustained receiver congestion.

tasks.title: Implement SFU node selection, health and failover
tasks.description: Select an SFU by region, capacity, supported features, room affinity and health. Define reconnect or migration behavior without silently weakening E2EE or permissions.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduling considers projected ingress, egress, participants, tracks, CPU and TURN usage.
Capacity claims are checked against observed metrics.
Unhealthy nodes stop receiving new rooms.
Failover creates a new routing/key epoch and rejects stale SFU tokens.
A room can recover through bounded reconnect or documented fallback.
Node identifiers and operational metrics do not expose plaintext media.

tasks.title: Add TURN-aware routing and relay cost controls
tasks.description: Detect relay usage, account for TURN ingress/egress amplification and apply bounded quality, admission or room-size policies when direct connectivity is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics distinguish direct, SFU and TURN-relayed bytes.
Admission can enforce configured relay bandwidth and cost ceilings.
TURN use never disables encryption or authentication.
Quality adaptation is per receiver.
Relay exhaustion triggers explicit degraded or rejected states.
Benchmarks include all-receivers-via-TURN worst-case scenarios.

tasks.title: Create room and broadcast observability without plaintext
tasks.description: Expose room topology, publications, subscriptions, layers, ingress, egress, TURN usage, congestion, drops, key epochs and fallback states using content-free telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics provide current and p50/p95/peak bandwidth per room and publication.
Ingress and egress are not conflated.
Per-receiver details are access-controlled and retention-bounded.
No transcript, media payload, speaker embedding or private key appears in telemetry.
Debug UI identifies why a receiver is degraded or on fallback.
Cardinality limits prevent participant IDs from overwhelming monitoring backends.

tasks.title: Add compatibility and deterministic topology fallback
tasks.description: Choose pair, mesh, SFU, control-only relay or standard media fallback using capabilities, room size, permissions, E2EE support and health.
acceptance_criteria: Identical inputs produce identical topology and reason codes.
Legacy clients remain in supported pair or standard-audio/video paths.
Fallback never silently grants publish, subscribe or decrypt permission.
Topology changes have bounded retry and cooldown behavior.
Control and transcript can survive media-topology degradation when policy permits.
Fallback capacity is tested at the maximum supported room size.

tasks.title: Create security, chaos and multi-room end-to-end tests
tasks.description: Test authorized and unauthorized publication, subscription, receiver-group changes, E2EE epochs, slow receivers, SFU loss, TURN-only networks, malicious payloads and concurrent rooms.
acceptance_criteria: A publisher uploads one stream/layer while multiple receivers obtain it.
Unauthorized receivers cannot subscribe or decrypt.
Removed participants lose future access after bounded rekey time.
One stalled receiver does not block other receivers.
SFU crash and reconnect reject stale routes, tokens and epochs.
Hub/SFU logs remain free of plaintext semantic, audio and video content under strict E2EE.

tasks.title: Benchmark 10, 25, 50, 100 and 250 receiver fan-out
tasks.description: Measure sender ingress, SFU egress, TURN traffic, CPU, memory, packets, latency, loss, recovery and semantic/control savings across ordinary media and optimized semantic modes.
acceptance_criteria: Scenarios include one publisher, several publishers, webinar, screen share, transcript broadcast and semantic reference fan-out.
Report includes median, p95 and peak rather than averages only.
Server egress is shown to scale with actual delivered receiver traffic.
Shared processing savings and network egress are reported separately.
Worst case includes standard encrypted media fallback and all receivers behind TURN.
Release limits are derived from reproducible measurements and documented infrastructure profiles.
Admission rejects or shards rooms before measured safe limits are exceeded.

definition_of_done: Existing two-peer WebRTC and Hub Relay behavior remains compatible.
One publisher can upload once to an SFU and at least 100 authorized receivers can subscribe under a documented infrastructure profile.
Each receiver can independently select quality and fallback without globally degrading the room.
Shared semantic and transcript payloads are fan-out optimized while personalized corrections and training data remain private.
Strict E2EE prevents SFU and Hub access to plaintext media and semantic content.
Join, leave, revoke, rekey, reconnect and SFU failover are deterministic and tested.
Queues, memory and buffered data remain bounded during slow-receiver and overload scenarios.
Metrics distinguish sender ingress, SFU egress, TURN relay, shared processing and receiver-specific traffic.
Benchmarks publish honest limits and include full ordinary-WebRTC fallback capacity.
